statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, against Stress 52 (elevated) on a rejected Iranian roadmap for the Strait of Hormuz, a ten-year Treasury yield at 5.18% near a two-decade high and an October Fed hike broadly priced into a PCE and payrolls week.
recommendation: Tail holds a 6-10 band and stays at least fifteen points below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls exactly at the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state. Existing-position management and protection are unaffected by the Tail mapping.
headline: CME weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while improving Gulf oil throughput trims Stress to 52 despite the rejected Hormuz roadmap
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday, exactly at the end of this forecast window, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 30,770.63 52-week high, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 within a 14.68-15.94 range and the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed at 51,828.62, 7,743.41 and 27,068.72 for weekly gains. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, so Tail is held at 6 and the mapped state is EA_ON. Stress eases two points to 52 on evidence that materially qualifies the weekend's headline. Washington has rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap, delivered through Qatar, which would have reopened the strait in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions, releasing roughly $12bn in frozen assets and a regional ceasefire, and President Pezeshkian has said Iran no longer trusts talks with Washington. Against that, tanker tracking cited on Saturday put crude leaving the Persian Gulf near 13 million barrels per day as of 24 September, roughly double a month earlier, after the US Navy cleared mines from the main corridor and shifted from night-only to daytime escorted transits. The strait is therefore still formally closed while actual throughput has improved sharply, which weakens the oil transmission channel into Nasdaq-100 risk relative to an assessment based on the diplomatic headline alone, and it gives Friday's oil easing - Brent settling 2.77% lower at 97.44, WTI November near 92.41 - a supply basis that does not simply reverse on Saturday's rejection. Reporting of privately held expectations of renewed strikes after the November midterms is a deferred rather than immediate risk. The rate backdrop is unchanged and heavy: the H.15 released 25 September shows, on 24 September data, the two-year at 4.87%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, with an effective fed funds rate of 3.88%, roughly two-thirds implied odds on a hike at the 28 October FOMC, and final September Michigan sentiment at 48.1, a four-month low, against that heavy rate path. August PCE and the final Q2 GDP print land on 30 September, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and September payrolls on 2 October. Tail therefore drifts from 6 to 10 across the window as unpriced weekend headlines accumulate into one reopening auction, which is discrete-event gap risk rather than the repeated extension after failed retracements that the elevated Tail band requires. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 20:11Z, which is more than ninety minutes before this assessment, so it is treated as stale; it also reported collectionStatus partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were used only as weak, non-real-time confirmation of Friday's orderly, chip-led tone and never as live NQ price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens at 22:00Z on Friday, an hour after the CME settlement, with Tail 10, Stress 49 and normal mode. Through Friday night and the early Saturday hours Tail decayed from 10 to 8 and Stress eased to a 44 trough. Across Saturday the halt held Tail in an 8 then 7 then 6 band while Stress rebuilt from 44 to 54 as the Hormuz diplomacy hardened and the rate backdrop stayed heavy, and Confidence drifted from 86 to 77 as the last tradable tape aged. Every hour in the window was mapped EA_ON and green, and no historical opinion has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: All twenty-four forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, exactly the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-10 band throughout and stays at least fifteen points below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The drift from 6 to 7 early on Sunday and to 8, 9 and then 10 through the afternoon is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of a single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure. Stress opens at 52, eases to a 49 overnight floor, firms as the Gulf working week and then the US Sunday programme window open, and caps at 56 late on Sunday; it stays two points below the previous hour's path throughout because tracked Gulf crude outflows near 13 million barrels per day under US-escorted transits weaken the oil channel that the closed-strait headline would otherwise imply. Confidence decays from 76 to 69 purely because the newest observable tape ages past seventy-two hours with no replacement possible before the reopen; the evidence base is otherwise complete on levels, yields, oil, volatility and the verified calendar.
